description: Solo or small-team build against a hard external deadline (hackathon, demo day). Correctness-critical core (e.g. concurrent/offline data sync) matters more than breadth. Cadence: one-shot before deadline, no ongoing release process. Cloud ceiling: effectively $0, must fit AWS always-free tier. No dedicated platform, security, or ops team — the builder(s) are all three.

anti_recommendations.microservices: kill — one team, one deadline, no second team to own a second service
anti_recommendations.kubernetes: kill — Lambda already manages the runtime, and there is no ops headcount to run a cluster
anti_recommendations.full-backend-framework-express-nestjs: kill — API Gateway already routes; a framework solves a long-lived-process problem this architecture doesn't have
anti_recommendations.orm-over-dynamodb: kill — DynamoDB access patterns are known and few; an ORM adds indirection with no real benefit at 4 tables
anti_recommendations.graphql: kill — small, well-defined API surface; REST + WebSocket covers every access pattern without a schema/resolver layer
anti_recommendations.sagemaker-or-trained-ml-model: kill — no training data exists yet at this stage; use Bedrock as a pre-trained foundation-model API call only, never model training
anti_recommendations.load-testing-beyond-demo-scale: warn — time spent here does not improve judging/demo outcomes; budget it last, if at all
anti_recommendations.multi-environment-cdk-before-core-is-sol: warn — dev/staging/prod separation is real engineering maturity but must not be built before the correctness-critical core passes its own rehearsal/test gate

named_approver_chain.stack_change: you (solo builder) — no committee at this scale, but write the decision down anyway
named_approver_chain.scope_addition_beyond_core: check against the project's own phased-scope document before adding — if it's not in Tier 1, it does not touch Tier 1's remaining build days
named_approver_chain.external-service-add: you — but confirm it's inside the AWS always-free tier before adding

canon_references: Shapiro, Preguica, Baquero & Zawirski, 'Conflict-free Replicated Data Types' (INRIA, 2011) — CRDT correctness properties, the basis for any PN-Counter/vector-clock design
Leslie Lamport, 'Time, Clocks, and the Ordering of Events in a Distributed System' (1978) — the original vector-clock / logical-time reasoning
AWS Well-Architected Framework — Serverless Applications Lens (2023) — idempotency, DLQs, and least-privilege IAM as default posture, not optional hardening
Werner Vogels, '10 Lessons from 10 Years of AWS' (2016) — build for the load you actually have, not hypothetical scale
Donald Reinertsen, Principles of Product Development Flow (2009) — minimize scope under a fixed deadline rather than a fixed budget
